text:
Philipp Grubauer has been doing a bit of everything for Seattle: starting, finishing games for Joey Daccord, and getting pulled himself once. He came on in relief on Nov. 7 and again on Nov. 14, when Daccord left after allowing four goals on 14 shots against Carolina, according to NHL.com's Tom Gulitti. Through 12 appearances he is 5-4-1 with an .893 save rate.

By our numbers he has been almost exactly as good as his shots: 32 goals allowed on 31.7 expected, so goals saved above expected (goals kept out beyond what the shots deserved) sits right around zero. The good news is rebound control. Only 7.9% of his saves lead to another shot within three seconds, against a league 10.8%. The concern is the hard chances, where his .667 trails the league's .685, and a recent stretch that has him 5.21 goals below expected over his last five games. Last season he finished 5.4 goals above expected in 32 games, so there is a better version of this season available. For now, the Kraken net looks like a shared job.
